SurveyCrawler comment: 'I am a seabed survey crawler. I know the position I am at, the direction I am facing, the sonar I use to know the ground I will end up on before moving or turning, and the run I am processing commands in. I process sequences of commands where each of a, t, h and g can be followed by a digit to be repeated, and where the commands written between parentheses are a guarded run: when one of them fails I undo the movements I made since the guarded run started.'.
CrawlerFacing comment: 'I am the direction a crawler faces. I know the displacement it does when it advances and which facing it gets when it turns.'.
CrawlerSonar comment: 'I am the sonar of a crawler. I know the ground of the seabed positions that were surveyed, answering firm sand for any other position.'.
SeabedGround comment: 'I am the ground of a seabed position. I decide how a crawler moves towards me and whether it can turn over me.'.
FirmSandGround comment: 'I am firm sand, the ground where a crawler moves and turns as expected.'.
SiltGround comment: 'I am silt, the ground where a crawler slides an unexpected number of cells, never further than my maximum sliding distance. I do not affect turning.'.
BoulderGround comment: 'I am a boulder, the ground a crawler can neither move to nor turn over.'.
CrawlerRun comment: 'I am the way a crawler is processing its commands. I decide whether the commands applied can be undone and whether the crawler is allowed to move over silt.'.
CrawlerUnguardedRun comment: 'I am the run of a crawler that is not being guarded. The commands I apply can not be undone and the crawler slides when it moves over silt.'.
CrawlerGuardedRun comment: 'I am the run of a crawler between an open parenthesis and a close parenthesis. I remember every command I apply so the crawler can go back to where the guarded run started when one of them fails. I do not let the crawler move over silt because sliding is unpredictable.'.
CrawlerCommand comment: 'I am a command a crawler processes. I know how to be applied to a crawler and how many times the command sequence says I have to be applied.'.
CrawlerRepeatableCommand comment: 'I am a command that can be followed by a digit in the command sequence, which says that I have to be applied that digit plus two more times.'.
FixedRandom comment: 'I answer always the same number, so tests can exercise the sliding of a crawler over silt.'.

CrawlerFacingDown comment: 'I am the facing of a crawler that advances downwards.'.
CrawlerFacingLeft comment: 'I am the facing of a crawler that advances to the left.'.
CrawlerFacingRight comment: 'I am the facing of a crawler that advances to the right.'.
CrawlerAdvanceCommand comment: 'I make a crawler advance one cell towards where it is facing.'.
CrawlerRetreatCommand comment: 'I make a crawler retreat one cell from where it is facing.'.
CrawlerTurnClockwiseCommand comment: 'I make a crawler turn clockwise.'.
CrawlerTurnCounterClockwiseCommand comment: 'I make a crawler turn counter clockwise.'.
CrawlerStartGuardedRunCommand comment: 'I make a crawler start a guarded run.'.
CrawlerEndGuardedRunCommand comment: 'I make a crawler finish the guarded run it is processing.'.
SurveyCrawlerTest comment: 'I test a seabed survey crawler processing commands over the grounds its sonar detects.'.
